prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has passed the subjects Manufacturing Engineering and Manufacturing Technologies.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are expected to be able to design manufacturing processes, from the geometric conception and modeling of elementary parts to obtaining the final product, based on computer-aided design and manufacturing technologies. Similarly, students will be provided with the necessary resources for simulating these processes and will know and apply, as far as possible, the most current manufacturing technologies.

Acquisition by the student of the basic knowledge that allows them to conveniently address problems related to establishing the optimal conditions necessary to carry out a given machining process. Similarly, the aim is for students to be introduced to special machining processes. In parallel, in more practical aspects, the student should acquire the necessary proficiency in handling conventional machine tools and be introduced to the programming of Numerical Control machine tools, as well as being able to evaluate the quality of a machined part. Additionally, it would be desirable to acquire sufficient knowledge to undertake tasks related to the organization of a Mechanical Workshop.

Acquisition by the student of basic knowledge that allows them to conveniently address problems related to establishing the optimal conditions necessary to carry out a specific manufacturing process that includes material forming processes with material conservation: selection and identification of technologies, equipment, and processes; design of the global process; analysis, evaluation, and improvement of process performance from economic, energy, and environmental viewpoints.

syllabus_topics: Conventional Machining Processes: Introduction, Theoretical Foundations, Performance of Conventional Processes, Machinability, Quality Criteria
Non-Conventional Machining Processes: Introduction, Theoretical Foundations, Performance of Non-Conventional Processes, Machinability, Quality Criteria
High-Performance Machining: Introduction, Concept of High Performance, Strategic Processes and Materials
CNC Programming: Introduction to Manual Programming, ISO Code / GCODE, Manual Programming, Conversational Programming, Post-processing

assessment_methods.method: Set of theoretical-practical activities proposed during the course

assessment_rules: The evaluation will be developed through a continuous assessment methodology, including a monographic work, a set of theoretical-practical activities, and a computer practical report. No specific grading formula or resit arrangements are detailed.
